# Ngo et al.'s symbolic transliterator, vendored

The Vietnamese symbolic transliterator from
[ngohgia/transliteration](https://github.com/ngohgia/transliteration) (MIT),
for Ngo, Chen, Sivadas, Ma and Li, *A Minimal-Resource Transliteration
Framework for Vietnamese*, Interspeech 2014.

Copied as-is apart from one change: fifteen Python 2 `print` statements are
now `print()` calls, so it runs under Python 3. No logic was touched.

It takes `word<TAB><TAB>phones`, one phone symbol per letter, `_` for a letter
with no sound, in a stress-free ARPAbet with allophones (AX, AXR, IX, DX, and
TD/DD/KD/PD/BD/GD for unreleased stops). It writes X-SAMPA with tone numbers.

    python3 transliterator.py input.lex output.txt

## This copy does not reproduce their results

Run on `data/ngo/large_test.lex`, which is their own input, this copy
reproduces their own shipped `large_test.output` for **28.4%** of 2,400
words. On the example in their paper, disneyland, the paper gives
`đi sờ ni len` and this copy gives `đi ni lan`, dropping the z instead of
making it a syllable.

So something is wrong, and it is not hash-seed order: the output is identical
across `PYTHONHASHSEED` 1, 2 and 3. The remaining candidates are the Python 2
to 3 conversion changing behaviour somewhere beyond the print statements, or
the shipped output having come from a different revision or configuration
than the files here.

Nothing in `app/` is generated by this copy. The playground shows only the
2,391 readings published in `data/ngo/`, which are theirs. This directory is
kept for the investigation, not for producing readings.
